facts.statement: The genus Otodus was first described by Louis Agassiz in 1843.
Fossils of Otodus range from the Paleocene epoch to the Early Pliocene epoch.
Otodus is an extinct genus of mackerel sharks that lived globally from the Paleocene to the Pliocene.
facts.quote: Otodus is an extinct, cosmopolitan genus of mackerel shark which lived from the Paleocene to the Pliocene epochs.

facts.statement: All Otodus species are known from fossilized teeth, while four species are also known from fossilized vertebrae.
facts.quote: All species are known from their fossilized teeth, and four of them (O. obliquus, O. auriculatus, O. angustidens and O. megalodon) are also known from their fossilized vertebral centra.

facts.statement: Estimates for the maximum length of O. megalodon vary between 20.3 meters and 24.3 meters.
facts.quote: Studies estimating the maximum body length of O. megalodon have varied, stating measurements ranging from approximately 20.3 m to 24.3 m (80 ft).

facts.statement: At least two Otodus species used warm-water coastal nursery areas to give birth to their young.
facts.quote: Like contemporaneous sharks, at least two species of Otodus (O. angustidens and O. megalodon) made use of nursery areas to birth their young in, specifically warm-water coastal environments with large amounts of food and protection from predators.

facts.statement: A potential nursery area for O. obliquus was found in the Ganntour basin in Morocco.
facts.quote: A possible nursery area of O. obliquus has been discovered in the Ganntour basin, Morocco.

facts.statement: Studies suggest a dietary shift from fish to marine mammals occurred in the evolutionary history of otodontid sharks, based on zinc enrichment patterns in their teeth.
facts.quote: Schwenk et al. (2026) compared zinc enrichment of the enameloid of Otodus obliquus and O. megalodon, finding evidence of higher concentrations of zinc in regions of teeth of O. megalodon which were affected by high stress during feeding and finding evidence of less pronounced spatial variation of zinc in O. obliquus, and interpret this finding as suggestive of a shift from a fish-based diet to a more marine mammal-based diet during the evolutionary history of otodontid sharks.

facts.statement: It is widely believed that Otodus originated from the genus Cretalamna due to similar tooth morphology.
facts.quote: It is widely believed that the genus originates from a lineage of sharks belonging to the genus Cretalamna, due to strong similarities in tooth morphology.

facts.statement: Scientists believe Otodus evolved into the genus Carcharocles based on transitional fossil teeth.
facts.quote: Scientists determined that Otodus evolved into the genus Carcharocles, given substantial fossil evidence in the form of transitional teeth.

facts.statement: The species O. debrayi lived from the Early Eocene to the Middle Eocene epoch.
facts.quote: Otodus debrayi is a species known to have lived from the Early Eocene to Middle Eocene epoch.

facts.statement: O. debrayi fossils date from 47.8 to 38 million years ago and have been found in Africa, North America, Central Asia, and Europe.
facts.quote: This species has been found in Africa, North America, Central Asia, and Europe, dating from 47.8 to 38 million years ago.

facts.statement: The controversial species O. poseidoni was first described in 1999 and measures approximately 12 meters.
facts.quote: Otodus poseidoni is a controversial species that was first described in 1999, measuring approximately 12 meters.

facts.statement: A species found in Kazakhstan is considered an undescribed species (nomen nudum) and is likely Otodus sp.
facts.quote: It is an undescribed species (nomen nudum),found in Kazakhstan, considered by most paleontologists to be Otodus sp..

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Otodus is the family Otodontidae.
Otodus belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
The time range for Otodus is from the Turonian to the Chibanian, spanning 93.9 to 0.34 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Chibanian (93.9 to 0.34 million years ago)
